related_questions.question: What percentage of children have adverse reactions to vaccines?

text_blocks.snippet: Adverse reactions to vaccines in children are generally rare, with most being mild and temporary. Severe reactions, like anaphylaxis, are extremely uncommon, occurring in about one in a million doses. Most common side effects are mild, like soreness at the injection site or a mild fever.

list.title: Mild Reactions:
list.snippet: These are common and include pain or swelling at the injection site, mild fever, fatigue, and headache.

list.title: Moderate Reactions:
list.snippet: Some children may experience more pronounced fever, fussiness, or loss of appetite.

list.title: Severe Reactions:
list.snippet: Severe reactions, such as anaphylaxis, are very rare.

list.title: Febrile Seizures:
list.snippet: A small percentage of children (around 1 in 3,000 to 4,000) might experience febrile seizures after certain vaccines like MMR.

list.title: MMR Vaccine:
list.snippet: About 1 in 6 children develop a fever after the MMR vaccine, and about 1 in 3,000 may experience febrile seizures.

list.title: COVID-19 Vaccine:
list.snippet: Most reported reactions were mild to moderate, with injection site pain, fatigue, and headache being the most common.

list.title: DTPa + Hib Vaccine:
list.snippet: Injection site reactions, like swelling and pain, are more common with this vaccine.
The vast majority of children experience no or only mild side effects from vaccines.
The benefits of vaccination far outweigh the small risk of adverse reactions.
